core_rule: Treat Marshalls as a network of defended air/lagoon/logistics nodes plus rear staging islands. Post-GALVANIC lessons change placement, survival and repair; they do not create untraced aircraft or concrete fortresses.

lesson_latency.0_7_days: Observable/simple lessons: lagoon-side assault, LVT reef crossing, protected stores/comms survive bombardment, massed exposed assets die, support shipping remains vulnerable.
lesson_latency.1_3_weeks: Procedural lessons: all-around fire plans, alternate command posts/wire, dispersed ammunition/water, tank concealment/mobile-firepoint use, pre-registered anti-LVT lanes, runway/water-air recovery teams.
lesson_latency.3_8_weeks: Physical conversion where shipping/material/terrain allow: additional secondary positions, revetments, protected stores, alternate ramps/taxiways, local reserve routes and deeper use of available terrain. No automatic cave network or major new concrete fortress.

nodes.post_Tarawa_change: Already strong; emphasize alternate revetments, dispersed fuel/ammunition, runway repair, secondary local positions and deception. Construction increasingly contested by US bombing from December.
Same outer-island expectation remains, so substantial reinforcement is rational; stronger fire-plan/secondary positions but atoll depth ceiling remains.
Hardening improves aircraft survival/repair and coastal/lagoon defense; close to new US Gilbert airfields, so repeated suppression becomes a major construction tax.
Separate runway and water-air facilities; alternate ramps, fuel, crane/support craft dispersal and local defense become high-value.

Largest qualitative ground-defense correction: lagoon-side assault is no longer abstract. Add all-around registered fires, local fallback positions, reserve routes, redundant C2/stores. Do not assume Japan correctly predicts direct Kwajalein leapfrog.
Prioritize dispersal, staging, fuel/repair and warning more than beach-fortress construction until threat sharpens.
Historical field was incomplete; Branch construction/logistics makes completion to useful staging status a major open gate. Do not credit large combat fighter force without a delivery/OOB ledger.
Useful in Truk->Ponape->Kusaie->Marshall chain; direct sustained fighter defense of Kwajalein is not centered.
Can threaten Kwajalein approaches with medium/long-range aircraft but is not a free fighter-CAP reservoir.
Raised-island hardening helps support system survival; supply and repeated US bombing limit sustained output.
Too far to behave as direct fighter base; feeds Marshalls through Eniwetok or Ponape/Kusaie staging chains and carries mobile fleet reserve.

shipping_reopen: Absolute Nov-1943 to Jan-1944 cargo/ship-day allocation is NOT closed here. Next gate must ledger bulk construction cargo, engineer plant, ammunition, communications, aviation support and garrison movements by route and arrival date.
guards: Do not use 1944 Marianas cave doctrine retroactively.
Do not turn staging range into simultaneous combat concentration.
Repeated US bombing reduces net construction output from mid-December onward.
